full_text_zh:
[P1] 元宵节的故事
连环画出版社

[P2] 元宵节的故事
司南/改编
励国仪/绘画

连环画出版社

东方朔是我国古代汉武帝时期的官员。他很有学问，头脑也非常灵活。

[P3] 有一年腊月，东方朔在御花园里游玩，发现一个宫女正在井边伤心地哭。东方朔赶紧跑过去，问她为什么这么难过。
这个宫女叫元宵。她来到皇宫好几年了，非常思念家人，但又不能回家，真觉得生不如死。东方朔安慰她：“姑娘，别难过了，我想办法让你见到家人。”

[P4] 东方朔来到元宵姑娘家中，对元宵的家人说：“我有个主意，能让元宵和你们团聚。”他仔细嘱咐元宵的妹妹，告诉她应该怎么做。
随后，东方朔打扮成一个算命先生，来到街头：“我夜观天象，京城要有一场大火灾！”老百姓纷纷求他化解灾难。东方朔说：“正月十三，有人骑黑驴，穿红衣，从南边过来，那就是火神君。大家要跪在路边苦苦求他，全城才能得救。”

[P5] 老百姓照东方朔的话去做。天快黑的时候，火神君真的
穿着红衣，从南边骑驴而来。
大家跪在路边向火神君求情。火神君扔下一封信，说：
“火烧京城是玉皇大帝的旨意！你们把这封信送到皇宫，交
给皇帝，或许能免去这场灾难。”

[P6] 有人拾起信，连夜送进了皇宫。
信上写着：“正月十六，火烧皇宫；要想消灾，汤圆花灯。”皇帝不明白是怎么回事，请来东方朔给他出主意。

[P7] 东方朔听了事情经过，对皇帝说：“听说火神君爱吃汤圆。正月十五那天，多让百姓做汤圆、扎花灯，求玉皇大帝和火神君不要降灾。”
皇帝听了，立刻让人传令：不管宫里宫外，大家都要多做汤圆，多扎花灯。

[P8] 元宵姑娘是做汤圆的能手。东方朔嘱咐她，让她扎一盏大大的花灯，写上自己的名字，字要写得大大的，让人一眼看得见。
正月十五这天，皇帝用元宵姑娘做的汤圆，供在火神君的画像前，求神仙保佑百姓平安。

[P9] 到了晚上，全城百姓都上街看花灯。元宵提着自己扎的花灯，也走在人群里。
元宵的妹妹搀扶着爸爸妈妈，也来到街上看花灯。她走着走着，忽然看见远处有一盏大花灯，上面写着姐姐的名字。

[P10] 妹妹大声喊：“元宵姐姐！元宵姐姐！”元宵听见喊声，连忙跑过来。见到日夜思念的亲人，元宵激动得哭了起来。
一家人都很感激东方朔。妹妹说：“东方先生的主意真好，让我装扮成火神君，咱们才能全家团聚！”

[P11] 百姓闹了一夜花灯，京城平安无事。皇帝十分高兴，下令第二年正月十五照样做汤圆，扎花灯，庆贺太平。
这个风俗一年一年传下来。因为正月十五上供的汤圆是元宵姑娘做的，所以汤圆从此也叫“元宵”，正月十五就叫做“元宵节”。

[P12] 在我国古代，元宵节是和新年同样重要的节日。在这一天，人们要吃元宵或汤圆，赏花灯，猜灯谜，举行种种庆祝活动。
元宵和汤圆有什么区别呢？元宵是先做好馅，再放到江米（即糯米）粉中去“摇”，让江米粉均匀地粘在馅上做成的；而汤圆是先用水和好江米粉，捏成皮，再像包饺子一样包进汤圆馅做成的。汤圆比元宵湿、软，个子也要小一些。北方人常吃元宵，南方人常吃汤圆。宁波的“黑洋酥”汤圆，馅料用猪油和黑芝麻粉混合而成，而且猪油一定要取猪肚子里的原块“板油”，用手慢慢揉搓、挤压，再一点点掺入黑芝麻粉，煮熟后吃起来滑、糯、香、软，十分可口。
元宵节又称“灯节”，与赏花灯的活动密切相连。明朝时，京城灯节前后一共十天，其中正月十六比十五更热闹：妇女夜晚结伴出游，称为“走百病”，据说这夜走一走，一年不得病。这
正月十五闹花灯的习俗也传了下来，人们在这一天展花灯，猜灯谜。所以，元宵节也叫“灯节”。

[P13] 一习俗在今天的华北一带仍然盛行。
京郊乡村人在十一日至十六日用秫秸秆布置灯阵，称为“黄河九曲灯”，似乎来自《封神演义》的传说，人们进入后稍不小心，真能迷路。房山人至今还保留“散灯花”的民俗：正月十五白天用红、黄、蓝、白、黑五色纸自制纸花，称为“捻灯花”，做完摆在大盘子中，蘸上香油或其他可食用的植物油，每家只做一盘；当天晚饭后两人同出，一人端盘子，一人手拿点燃的蜡烛，另一手用筷子夹起灯花在蜡烛上点燃，从正房里屋到外屋，然后到院里，再到院外地散放，灯花之间的距离和先后方向都有一定之规。有的人家散完灯花后还要放鞭炮，到处都明亮而热闹。
福建和台湾等地的年轻未婚女性有在元宵夜偷摘葱、菜的传统习俗，偷到葱、菜预示婚姻幸福美满；小孩子会互相扔石子，称为“掷石”，据说如果不这样做，当年就会发生瘟疫。湖南有些地方在灯火游行后，会将龙灯烧掉，称为“送灾”。
元宵节是春节过后的狂欢，人们在这时用各种仪式和活动祈求婚姻美满、子嗣旺盛、身体健康与田地丰收，迎接美好的新年。
full_text_en:
[P1] The Story of the Lantern Festival
Lianhuanhua Publishing House

[P2] The Story of the Lantern Festival
Adapted by Si Nan
Illustrated by Li Guoyi

Lianhuanhua Publishing House

Dongfang Shuo was an official during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty in ancient China. He was very learned and had a very quick mind.

[P3] One winter month, Dongfang Shuo was strolling in the imperial garden when he discovered a palace maid crying sadly by a well. He hurried over and asked her why she was so sad.
This palace maid was named Yuanxiao. She had been in the palace for several years, deeply missing her family, yet unable to return home. She felt life was not worth living. Dongfang Shuo comforted her: "Girl, don't be sad. I'll find a way to help you see your family."

[P4] Dongfang Shu came to Yuanxiao's home and told her family, "I have an idea that can reunite Yuanxiao with you." He carefully instructed Yuanxiao's younger sister, telling her what to do.
Later, Dongfang Shu disguised himself as a fortune-teller and went to the street: "I observed the stars last night; the capital will suffer a great fire!" The common people rushed to him, begging for help to avert the disaster. Dongfang Shu said, "On the 13th day of the first lunar month, someone riding a black donkey, wearing red clothes, will come from the south. That is the Fire God. Everyone must kneel by the roadside and beg him earnestly, only then can the whole city be saved."

[P5] The common people followed Dongfang Shuo's advice. As dusk approached, the Fire God truly
appeared, wearing red robes, riding a donkey from the south.
Everyone knelt by the roadside to beg the Fire God for mercy. The Fire God threw down a letter, saying:
"The burning of the capital is the decree of the Jade Emperor! Take this letter to the imperial palace and hand it to the emperor; perhaps this disaster can be averted."

[P6] Someone picked up the letter and delivered it to the palace overnight.
The letter read: "On the sixteenth day of the first month, the imperial palace will burn; to avert disaster, eat tangyuan and light lanterns." The emperor didn't understand what was going on, so he summoned Dongfang Shuo to give him advice.

[P7] Dongfang Shuo, after hearing the story, said to the emperor, "I heard that the God of Fire loves to eat tangyuan. On the 15th day of the first lunar month, let the people make more tangyuan and lanterns, and pray to the Jade Emperor and the God of Fire not to bring disaster." 
The emperor, upon hearing this, immediately ordered: whether inside or outside the palace, everyone must make more tangyuan and more lanterns.

[P8] Yuanxiao was good at making tangyuan. Dongfang Shuo instructed her to make a big lantern, write her name on it, and make the characters large so everyone could see them.
On the 15th day of the first lunar month, the emperor offered the tangyuan made by Yuanxiao in front of the portrait of the Fire God, praying for the safety of the people.

[P9] In the evening, all the people in the city went out to watch the lanterns. Yuanxiao carried the lantern she had made and walked among the crowd.
Yuanxiao's younger sister, supporting her parents, also came to the street to watch the lanterns. As she walked, she suddenly saw a large lantern in the distance with her sister's name written on it.

[P10] The younger sister shouted loudly: "Sister Yuanxiao! Sister Yuanxiao!" Yuanxiao heard the call and rushed over. Seeing her long-missed family, Yuanxiao burst into tears.
Everyone in the family was very grateful to Dongfang Shuo. The younger sister said: "Mr. Dongfang's idea was brilliant. Letting me disguise as the Fire God is how we were able to reunite as a family!"

[P11] The people celebrated with lanterns all night, and the capital remained safe. The emperor was very happy and ordered that the next year on the 15th day of the first lunar month, they would still make tangyuan and make lanterns to celebrate peace.
This custom was passed down year after year. Since the tangyuan offered on the 15th day of the first lunar month were made by the girl Yuanxiao, tangyuan came to be called 'yuanxiao', and the 15th day of the first lunar month became known as the 'Yuanxiao Festival'.

[P12] In ancient China, the Lantern Festival was as important as the New Year. On this day, people eat yuanxiao or tangyuan, admire lanterns, guess lantern riddles, and hold various celebrations.
What's the difference between yuanxiao and tangyuan? Yuanxiao is made by first preparing the filling, then placing it into glutinous rice (i.e., sticky rice) powder and "shaking" it until the powder evenly coats the filling. Tangyuan, on the other hand, is made by first mixing glutinous rice flour with water, kneading it into a dough, and then wrapping the filling inside like dumplings. Tangyuan is moister, softer, and smaller than yuanxiao. People in the north often eat yuanxiao, while those in the south prefer tangyuan. Ningbo's "Hei Yang Su" tangyuan uses lard and black sesame powder as filling. The lard must be taken from the original block of "board lard" inside the pig's belly, then slowly kneaded and pressed by hand, with black sesame powder gradually added. When cooked, it is smooth, glutinous, fragrant, and soft, very delicious.
The Lantern Festival is also called the "Festival of Lanterns," closely linked to the activity of admiring lanterns. During the Ming Dynasty, the capital's lantern festival lasted ten days, with the 16th of the first lunar month being even more lively than the 15th: women would go out in groups at night, a practice called "Zou Bai Bing," said to prevent illness for the whole year.
The custom of celebrating with lanterns on the 15th of the first lunar month has been passed down. On this day, people display lanterns and guess riddles. Therefore, the Lantern Festival is also called the "Festival of Lanterns."

[P13] One custom still prevails in northern China today.
In the suburbs of Beijing, villagers set up light arrays using straw stalks from the 11th to the 16th, called the "Yellow River Nine-Bend Lanterns," seemingly originating from the legend in "Investiture of the Gods." People entering it might easily get lost. In Fangshan, people still preserve the folk custom of "scattering lantern flowers": on the 15th of the first lunar month, they make paper flowers using red, yellow, blue, white, and black paper, called "twisting lantern flowers," place them in large trays, dip them in sesame oil or other edible plant oil, and each family makes only one tray; after dinner, two people go out together, one carrying the tray, the other holding a lit candle, and using chopsticks to pick up the paper flowers and ignite them on the candle, moving from the inner room to the outer room, then to the yard, and finally to the area outside the yard, with specific rules for the distance and order of the flowers. Some families also set off firecrackers after scattering the flowers, making the whole place bright and lively.
In Fujian, Taiwan, and other areas, young unmarried women have the traditional custom of secretly picking green onions and vegetables on the night of the Lantern Festival; stealing onions and vegetables is believed to foretell a happy and fulfilling marriage; children throw stones at each other, called "stone throwing," and it is said that if they don't do this, an epidemic will occur that year. In some places in Hunan, after the lantern parade, they burn the dragon lanterns, called "sending away disasters."
The Lantern Festival is a carnival after the Spring Festival, during which people use various rituals and activities to pray for happy marriages, abundant offspring, good health, and bountiful harvests, welcoming a wonderful new year.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本封面，标题为《元宵节的故事》，由连环画出版社出版，画面描绘了三位身着古装的女子、舞龙、灯笼和热闹的节日场景，展现了元宵节的喜庆氛围。
[P2] 本页为绘本第2页，左侧是封面信息，右侧插图描绘了东方朔在月光下与仙鹤相伴的场景，并配文介绍他是汉武帝时期的官员，有学问且头脑灵活。
[P3] 东方朔在御花园发现宫女元宵在井边哭泣，上前询问原因，并安慰她会想办法让她与家人团聚。
[P4] 东方朔来到元宵的家中，向其家人提出团聚的主意，并嘱咐元宵的妹妹。随后，他装扮成算命先生，在街头散布京城将有火灾的预言，并告知百姓如何祈求火神君以化解灾难。
[P5] 本页描绘了百姓按照东方朔的计策行事，火神君现身并留下一封信，声称火烧京城是玉皇大帝的旨意，需将信送至皇宫以求免灾。
[P6] 有人连夜将火神君留下的信送入皇宫，信中预言正月十六皇宫将遭火灾，唯有汤圆花灯可消灾，皇帝因此召见东方朔商议对策。
[P7] 东方朔向皇帝建议在正月十五让百姓做汤圆、扎花灯以祈求免灾，皇帝随即下令宫内外都要多做汤圆、多扎花灯。
[P8] 东方朔嘱咐元宵姑娘制作一盏写有自己名字的大花灯，皇帝则在正月十五用她做的汤圆供奉火神君，祈求百姓平安。
[P9] 元宵节当晚，全城百姓上街赏灯，元宵提着自己制作的花灯在人群中行走；她的妹妹搀扶着父母也来赏灯，意外发现一盏写有姐姐名字的大花灯。
[P10] 元宵的妹妹在灯会中认出姐姐并呼喊，元宵激动相认，一家人团聚；妹妹感谢东方朔的计策，称其装扮成火神君才促成团圆。
[P11] 本页讲述了元宵节的由来：百姓燃灯祈福后京城平安，皇帝下令延续此习俗，因汤圆由元宵姑娘所做，故汤圆得名“元宵”，正月十五也被称为“元宵节”。
[P12] 本页介绍了元宵节的传统习俗，包括吃元宵或汤圆、赏花灯、猜灯谜，并解释了元宵与汤圆的制作区别及地域差异，同时说明了元宵节又称“灯节”的由来。
[P13] 本页介绍了中国各地元宵节的多样民俗，包括华北地区的黄河九曲灯、房山的散灯花，福建台湾的偷葱偷菜、掷石，以及湖南的送灾等习俗，并总结元宵节是祈求婚姻、子嗣、健康与丰收的节日。
